hook: SCP-469 is a huge ball of white wings with something curled up at its centre, and it feeds on sound. The containment section reads like library rules taken to an extreme, and that enforced silence is the setup for everything after it. Do not skip the footnotes; the incident turns on a very ordinary human slip.
whyItMatters: The article sets an angelic, beautiful image beside a cruel way of feeding and never tries to reconcile the two. It is also a tidy example of a defence that feeds on attack: the noise of most weapons is exactly what makes the creature grow back faster. And it gives a Keter entity that has killed several people an ending that reads like grief, which is a less common note to finish on.
thingsToNotice:
The feeding is described plainly. Anyone who gets close is wrapped in wings, the sharp barbs inject stimulants that switch on every pain receptor while keeping the victim awake, and the screaming feeds the creature until the person bleeds out or suffocates under new growth; four personnel died that way and two agents more when cutting tools were tried, while flamethrowers failed because the roar of the fire was food.

Incident 469-01 happens because a researcher muted her phone as required but had set her wake-up alarm to the evening by mistake, and the alarm tone was a bell, the sound the creature likes best. It armours itself in its own wings, rips up through every floor, and launches skyward at more than 1200 mph, but each wingbeat sheds feathers, and by the fifth it has lost about half and drops into a forest roughly 1.2 km away, still clawing at the sky. Back in containment it curls up again, and researchers report something like muffled crying from inside.
